judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates route and shift rules outside the reorganisation paragraphs (c020, c021) and outside the tailman staffing assumptions there ('such routes will not require a tailman'); the fit is loose but I found no direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Will make every effort within its control to insure that the NMDU's jurisdiction ... is protected' is a best-efforts promise with no standard, and 'bootlegging' is never defined. Both are nameable and the clause may be aspirational only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers jurisdiction to 'the Collective Bargaining Agreement' extended by c001 rather than defining it here; nothing else in the instrument addresses bootlegging, so no direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete deadline and a fixed committee composition; only the phrase 'the appropriate workforce' is soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contemplates transfers to 43rd Street, which the new-and-rebuilt-facilities letter (c064) excludes from the Memorandum's facility provisions; the two touch but do not clearly conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Specifically charged with administering the transfer process' states a remit without any decision-making power, deadlines or deadlock rule. Mildly vague but short and unremarkable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds nothing beyond c072 and does not displace the vacancy-filling procedures in the separate side letter (c076-c080); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanism is internally awkward: contributions made in calendar year 1996 reduce an obligation, and 'said reductions will be evenly distributed throughout the calendar years 1992, 1993, 1994, and 1995' — a retroactive spreading of a figure not knowable until 1996. That is a concrete drafting defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 3-A(3) (c011) fixes a minimum of 450 FTEs for 1992-1995 and says nothing about 1996, while side letter c069 increases the same figure and c066 requires additional contributions; the four texts adjust one obligation in opposite directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to take unspecified 'steps necessary to effectuate amendments' — an agreement to agree, with no standard for what amendments are 'necessitated.' Mildly nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly serves paragraph 3-A(3) (c011) and the same letter (c074); it is facilitative rather than in tension with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'On an inverse seniority basis, to assign the most junior qualified situation holder' leaves 'qualified' undefined and 'pending final award' undated, and the sentence describes both parties as agreeing to assign. Nameable but modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be squared with c078, which requires the Chapel Chairman volunteer step 'prior to instituting the procedure above,' and with the seniority bidding rights in 4.D (c019) and inverse-seniority utilisation in Appendix A, C (c056).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph says junior holders 'shall be restored to their former situation' at the end of a temporary situation and then that they 'shall be permanently assigned to permanent or vacant positions in the event those situations are not filled by bid' — two outcomes for the same person without a stated priority. That is a nameable internal tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same permanent-assignment rule reappears in c078's closing sentence with the added consequence that 'the volunteer shall return to his regular situation'; the two statements of the rule are not identically framed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sequencing is confusing — a volunteer must be supplied and must fill the situation within seven days, yet the vacancy is then permanently assigned to the most junior qualified holder 'in the event the situation is not filled by bid,' with no rule for when a volunteer has filled it. Nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says it must occur 'prior to instituting the procedure above,' which reverses the order in which c076 and c077 are written, and it duplicates c077's permanent-assignment sentence with a different consequence for the volunteer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any temporary vacancy which is foreseen to be of two (2) weeks or less duration' turns on who foresees and when, and there is no rule for a vacancy that overruns the forecast. That is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It exempts the procedures in c076-c078 without saying what applies instead to short vacancies; the gap is a loose end rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The option to fill any vacancies created as a result of the assignment' is a plain discretionary right, though 'option' leaves the alternative unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with 4.D (c019), under which vacated situations may be filled or eliminated at The Times' discretion subject to manning requirements; the two are broadly aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The NMDU may, within 72 hours, discuss the possibility of employment opportunities' creates at most a right to talk, with the 72 hours running from an unspecified point and no obligation on The Times. The provision may be argued to promise nothing at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument addresses hiring from other newspapers, and it does not touch the RSH list mechanics in paragraph 4 (c016, c017); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A named individual, a named position, fixed days off and a fixed start time; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a one-off settlement that does not engage the bidding, seniority or vacancy provisions elsewhere in the instrument in any obvious way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, definite undertaking to withdraw a grievance with prejudice, with the consideration recited. Plain words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the counterpart of c082 and does not bear on the grievance and arbitration machinery in paragraph 2 (c005-c007); no conflict found.
